- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to account for risk/reversal.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days > 85% of historical mean), model fails to adjust; apply downward bias.
- If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sudden drop, model misses reversal; add early warning buffer (e.g., -2% if sentiment turns negative).
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in late period; increase forecast by 1–2% for last 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match sentiment swing direction.
